Frozen task/task.toml [environment] (lines 20-24) contains only build_timeout_sec = 600.0, network_mode = "public", cpus = 2, memory_mb = 4096; no docker_image key. Grep for 'docker_image|image\s*=' over the entire frozen task tree returns no matches, so no other file (environment/, tests/, solution/) sets a prebuilt image. diff against the frozen template task.toml shows only task-specific [task]/[metadata] text changes (name, description, keywords, difficulty, difficulty_explanation, category, provenance, arena_slice); [agent], [environment], [verifier], [verifier.env], [verifier.environment] are byte-identical to the template. The agent Dockerfile does have active build steps (task/environment/Dockerfile:5-23: apt-get install, npm install -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1, COPY instructions/ and assets/, chmod, git init/commit of /app), so they are live and not shadowed. task/environment/Dockerfile sha256 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1 equals the frozen template Dockerfile hash, i.e. template-controlled file preserved. environment/ contains only Dockerfile, assets/seed_data.json, instructions/{hireops_rules.md,integration.md}; no compose file or alternate image config. Adversarial consideration: if docker_image were set, the agent would start without /instructions, /assets/seed_data.json, the global express/better-sqlite3 install and the git-initialised /app, so a conforming agent could fail through no fault of its own; that shadowing does not occur here. A broken app cannot exploit this row (it is pure config wiring, independent of the submission).
